correctness.rationale: For quadratic \(g\), the proximal map is affine with matrix \(P=(I+\gamma B)^{-1}\). Substitution into the source normal residual gives the affine map \(R_\gamma^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=(A+B)P(z-\gamma b)+(a+b)\), whose Jacobian is invertible because \(A+B\succ0\) and \(P\) is invertible. Exact Newton therefore moves the normal-residual argument directly toward its zero. After scaling by \(\theta\), affineness of the proximal map gives \(\hat x^+=x_\star+(1-\theta)(y-x_\star)\). Quadratic energy scales by \((1-\theta)^2\), so \(\theta\in[0,2]\) never makes the candidate worse than the proximal-gradient fallback; the source decrease lemma then proves full-step acceptance. The scalar smooth example gives the exact line-search inequality and proves sharpness outside the interval.

value.rationale: The enlarged interval \((0,2/L_f)\) is a highlighted contribution of PANOC-lite, but the paper's most explicit Dennis--Moré superlinear specialization is stated on the older \((0,1/L_f)\) range. The finding shows that on the canonical strongly convex quadratic-composite class the Newton branch is not merely compatible with the doubled range: it accepts full steps globally, solves exactly at unit scaling, and tolerates any scalar overrelaxation up to a sharp factor of two. This identifies a concrete robustness margin for Newton-system inexact scaling and clarifies that the enlarged global stepsize range need not trade away fast-direction acceptance on this structural model.
